zeek_conn_log.title: Zeek conn.log
zeek_conn_log.definition: The connection log in Zeek summarizing Layer 3/4 session facts (IPs, ports, protocol, duration, byte counts, and connection state).
zeek_conn_log.context: Focuses on transport summaries. It does not carry application payloads or HTTP bodies.

api_endpoint.title: API Endpoint
api_endpoint.definition: A specific URI or path on a web server where client software sends structured requests to consume backend services.
api_endpoint.context: Reaching an API endpoint verifies network delivery; it does not indicate whether authorization succeeded.

json_payload.title: JSON Payload
json_payload.definition: A lightweight, text-based data format used to structure application responses between web servers and clients.
json_payload.context: Contained inside the HTTP application body; completely unobservable when sessions are encrypted.

user_agent_string.title: User-Agent String
user_agent_string.definition: An HTTP header string sent by the client identifying its software application, version, and operating system.
user_agent_string.context: Client-controlled and trivially spoofed; never use User-Agent alone as an indicator of authenticity.

packet_capture.title: Packet Capture (.pcap)
packet_capture.definition: A raw, byte-level file recording every frame that traversed a network interface or tap during the capture window.
packet_capture.context: Highest fidelity source available, but perishable due to high disk volume and rolling buffers.

tcp_handshake.title: TCP 3-Way Handshake
tcp_handshake.definition: The SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK sequence establishing a reliable transport connection between client and server sockets.
tcp_handshake.context: Proves transport connectivity only; tells you nothing about application authorization or status.

tcp_stream.title: TCP Stream
tcp_stream.definition: The full bidirectional sequence of ordered TCP segments belonging to a single 4-tuple socket conversation.
tcp_stream.context: In Wireshark, 'Follow TCP Stream' reconstructs payload bytes in chronological order.

ephemeral_port.title: Ephemeral Port
ephemeral_port.definition: A short-lived, high-numbered client source port (typically 49152–65535) dynamically assigned by the OS.
ephemeral_port.context: Identifies distinct client sockets; servers assign responses back to this port.

dns_resolver.title: Recursive DNS Resolver
dns_resolver.definition: A DNS server that accepts queries from clients and queries authoritative nameservers recursively to find the IP address.
dns_resolver.context: Workstations query resolvers; an edge sensor sees only traffic leaving or entering that resolver boundary.

dns_ttl.title: DNS TTL (Time to Live)
dns_ttl.definition: A 32-bit field in a DNS resource record defining how many seconds a client or resolver may cache the answer.
dns_ttl.context: Clients reuse cached entries until TTL expires, so subsequent connections generate no observable network queries.

cname_record.title: CNAME Record
cname_record.definition: A Canonical Name DNS record that maps an alias hostname to another true domain name in a lookup chain.
cname_record.context: Common in CDNs; lookups follow the chain until reaching an A or AAAA address record.

dns_cache.title: DNS Cache
dns_cache.definition: Temporary local memory where an operating system or browser stores recent DNS answers to avoid repeat queries.
dns_cache.context: Absence of a DNS query on the wire during a connection window is frequently explained by local cache hits.

server_name_indication.title: Server Name Indication (SNI)
server_name_indication.definition: A TLS extension in ClientHello where the client sends the destination hostname in cleartext before encryption begins.
server_name_indication.context: Visible on the wire unless Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) is deployed; client-controllable and can be decoyed.

tls_supported_versions.title: supported_versions Extension
tls_supported_versions.definition: TLS Extension 43 that communicates the true negotiated TLS version (0x0304 for TLS 1.3), bypassing legacy fields.
tls_supported_versions.context: Outer TLS version fields are frozen at 0x0303 (TLS 1.2) for middlebox compatibility.

middlebox.title: Middlebox
middlebox.definition: An inline network appliance (proxy, legacy firewall, or traffic shaper) that inspects or manipulates traffic.
middlebox.context: Legacy middleboxes dropping unknown version numbers forced TLS 1.3 to freeze legacy version headers.

self_signed_cert.title: Self-Signed Certificate
self_signed_cert.definition: An X.509 certificate whose digital signature is created by its own private key rather than a trusted CA.
self_signed_cert.context: Subject equals issuer; common in lab and staging environments, but unverified by public trust stores.

netflow_sampling.title: Sampled NetFlow
netflow_sampling.definition: A telemetry protocol exporting flow statistical summaries at a fixed sampling ratio (such as 1:100 packets).
netflow_sampling.context: Excellent for long-term volume trends; silence is weak evidence of absence for small, low-volume flows.

vpn_hairpin.title: Corporate VPN Gateway
vpn_hairpin.definition: A network boundary where traffic enters an encrypted tunnel, often undergoing address translation and routing changes.
vpn_hairpin.context: Edge firewalls see the gateway's public IP rather than the true internal workstation RFC 1918 address.

rolling_pcap_buffer.title: Rolling PCAP Buffer
rolling_pcap_buffer.definition: A finite disk ring buffer continuously recording raw packet bytes until storage limits force overwriting oldest files.
rolling_pcap_buffer.context: Retention is often 24–72 hours; always pull raw capture evidence against the shortest clock first.

discriminating_pair.title: Discriminating Inquiry
discriminating_pair.definition: An analytical method identifying an observation that must be present under one hypothesis and absent under another.
discriminating_pair.context: Separates competing explanations without gathering unnecessary, expensive data.

tcp_rst_ack.title: [RST, ACK] Packet
tcp_rst_ack.definition: A transport refusal packet indicating the destination host received the SYN, but rejected the socket attempt.
tcp_rst_ack.context: Proves the path and host are 100% reachable bidirectionally; points to host policy or closed ports.

conn_state_s0.title: connection.state: S0
conn_state_s0.definition: Zeek connection state where an opening SYN was observed, but zero response bytes or ACKs ever returned.
conn_state_s0.context: Indicates delivery failure (silent firewall drop or routing dead-end), resulting in client timeout.

path_mtu.title: Path MTU
path_mtu.definition: The maximum transmission unit size in bytes that can traverse an end-to-end network path without fragmentation.
path_mtu.context: Exceeding Path MTU forces IP fragmentation; intermediate drops of fragments break reassembly silently.

non_initial_fragment.title: Non-Initial Fragment
non_initial_fragment.definition: Subsequent IP packet fragments (offset > 0) carrying only payload bytes and lacking Layer 4 transport headers.
non_initial_fragment.context: Invisible to port-based firewall filters; policies dropping non-initial fragments cause silent timeouts.

c2_beaconing.title: C2 Beaconing
c2_beaconing.definition: Recurring, scheduled outbound network connections initiated by an implant to check in with a command server.
c2_beaconing.context: Shared by legitimate software (updates, NTP, NTP, telemetry); timing regularity alone is never proof of malice.

dns_tunneling.title: DNS Tunneling
dns_tunneling.definition: An evasion technique encoding non-DNS payloads or commands into subdomains and TXT response records.
dns_tunneling.context: Characterized by high-entropy subdomain strings, long query lengths, and caching bypass.

apex_domain.title: Apex Domain
apex_domain.definition: The base root domain (e.g. example.com) directly under a TLD, common across subdomains and distinct IPs.
apex_domain.context: Reveals relational convergence across seemingly independent IPs and protocols.

relational_convergence.title: Relational Convergence
relational_convergence.definition: Superficially independent network behaviors (HTTP poll, DNS bursts, uploads) connecting to a common entity.
relational_convergence.context: Much harder for adversaries to disguise than timing jitter; far stronger evidence than isolated shapes.

proportionate_action.title: Proportionate Action
proportionate_action.definition: A response whose severity and disruption match the strength of evidence and reversibility of the decision.
proportionate_action.context: Prevents overreacting (unnecessary reimaging) while maintaining containment of genuine risks.

confidence_breaker.title: Confidence Breaker
confidence_breaker.definition: A specifically named observation or test result that would immediately falsify the leading hypothesis.
confidence_breaker.context: Ensures an assessment is falsifiable and safe to be wrong in.

action_reversibility.title: Action Reversibility
action_reversibility.definition: The ease with which an operational intervention (like route rollback vs host reimage) can be safely undone.
action_reversibility.context: High reversibility enables swift operational remediation under uncertainty.

two_audience_handoff.title: Two-Audience Handoff
two_audience_handoff.definition: Delivering identical evidence claim strength to technical peers and managers while tailoring operational depth.
two_audience_handoff.context: Never adapt the certainty of a claim to leadership's appetite for a simple answer.

staged_c2_channel.title: Staged C2 Channel
staged_c2_channel.definition: A multi-phase connection where initial check-ins use decoy domains or small payloads before exfiltration begins.
staged_c2_channel.context: Designed to blend into normal post-update telemetry traffic.

immediate_containment.title: Immediate Containment
immediate_containment.definition: Network isolation of an endpoint to stop egress communication while preserving volatile memory (RAM).
immediate_containment.context: Crucial distinction: sever network access, but do not reboot or power off the endpoint.

model_revision.title: Model Revision Out Loud
model_revision.definition: The professional capability to publicly discard a previous hypothesis when contradictory evidence appears.
model_revision.context: The antidote to cognitive anchoring and defending failed models under management pressure.

decoy_sni.title: Decoy SNI
decoy_sni.definition: Crafting cleartext Server Name Indication fields requesting trusted company hostnames to fool egress monitoring.
decoy_sni.context: SNI is unauthenticated on the wire; an adversary's client can send any string in ClientHello.

conn_state_sf.title: connection.state: SF
conn_state_sf.definition: Normal SYN/FIN completion in Zeek; both sides cleanly opened and closed the connection.
conn_state_sf.context: Proves transport reachability and orderly socket teardown in both directions.

duration_microsecond.title: Sub-millisecond Duration
duration_microsecond.definition: Session elapsed time recorded in seconds; sub-millisecond durations indicate automated programmatic execution.
duration_microsecond.context: A duration like 0.000184s (184 µs) proves automated software speed rather than human typing.

http_403.title: 403 Forbidden
http_403.definition: HTTP status code where the server understood the request but actively refused to authorize it.
http_403.context: Proves the network path and web server are operational; the refusal originates in application authorization.

http_200.title: 200 OK
http_200.definition: HTTP status code indicating the web server successfully accepted and processed the request.
http_200.context: Confirms the HTTP exchange succeeded; does not prove whether the payload was the full dataset or just a metadata summary.

layer_independence.title: Layer Independence
layer_independence.definition: The principle that transport success (TCP) says nothing about application authorization (HTTP), and vice versa.
layer_independence.context: Avoid conflating layer statuses: a successful handshake does not mean an authorized request.

client_demarcation.title: Client Demarcation
client_demarcation.definition: Determining which host originated a conversation by identifying which socket sent the initial SYN frame.
client_demarcation.context: Crucial for determining conversation initiator versus responder, regardless of port numbers.

tcp_ack.title: TCP Acknowledgment
tcp_ack.definition: The receiver's TCP stack confirming receipt of bytes, independent of whether the application has processed or answered.
tcp_ack.context: A bare ACK proves network delivery to the host OS; application think time happens after.

falsifiable_prediction.title: Falsifiable Prediction
falsifiable_prediction.definition: An explicit, written commitment stating what specific network behavior must occur next if a hypothesis is true.
falsifiable_prediction.context: Writing down predictions before checking subsequent packets prevents hindsight bias.

connection_reset.title: Connection Reset (RST)
connection_reset.definition: An abrupt termination frame sent by an endpoint indicating rejection, teardown, or abnormal closure.
connection_reset.context: A reset is an explicit event with an origin; silence is an absence of observation.

reasoned_revision.title: Reasoned Revision
reasoned_revision.definition: Updating an analytical model based on contradictory evidence rather than rationalizing surprise or defending the previous model.
reasoned_revision.context: Distinguishes disciplined investigation from guessing or defending ego.

content_type_23.title: Content Type 23 (Application Data)
content_type_23.definition: TLS record type that encapsulates all post-ServerHello handshake messages and application payloads in TLS 1.3.
content_type_23.context: In TLS 1.3, certificates and extensions are encrypted under Content Type 23.

version_freeze.title: TLS Version 0x0303 Freeze
version_freeze.definition: The legacy outer record layer version field frozen at TLS 1.2 to prevent legacy middleboxes from dropping connections.
version_freeze.context: Negotiated TLS 1.3 versions are carried inside the supported_versions extension.

dropped_pipeline_fields.title: Dropped Pipeline Fields
dropped_pipeline_fields.definition: Log fields that exist on network sensors like Zeek but are discarded during ingestion before reaching the SIEM search index.
dropped_pipeline_fields.context: Never confuse what the tool pipeline happens to store with what the network actually carried.

bounded_claim.title: 3-Column Bounded Claim
bounded_claim.definition: Analytical method separating what is directly observable, what is inferable, and what cannot be determined without host telemetry.
bounded_claim.context: Prevents overreaching and identifies exactly which external data source to consult next.

conn_state_rej.title: connection.state: REJ
conn_state_rej.definition: Zeek connection state indicating active transport refusal; server OS responded immediately with an RST packet.
conn_state_rej.context: Proves bidirectional reachability; the server host is alive and actively refusing the connection.

conn_state_rstr.title: connection.state: RSTR
conn_state_rstr.definition: Zeek connection state indicating established session aborted by responder; server returned partial data then sent reset.
conn_state_rstr.context: Common when application workers crash or timeouts sever the server-side socket.

frame_15_proof.title: Immediate TCP ACK
frame_15_proof.definition: Immediate TCP ACK confirming instant network delivery before application think time begins.
frame_15_proof.context: Separates network latency (< 1ms) from application latency (4+ seconds).

exponential_backoff.title: Exponential Backoff
exponential_backoff.definition: Client TCP stack doubling retransmission delays across silence (1s, 2s, 4s) when packets are dropped.
exponential_backoff.context: A classic hallmark of silent path drops or dead-end firewall rules.

falsifiable_hypothesis.title: Falsifiable Hunting Hypothesis
falsifiable_hypothesis.definition: A structured proposition asserting that if a specific adversary behavior is occurring, named telemetry fields will exhibit an observable footprint—with explicit criteria that prove the hypothesis false.
falsifiable_hypothesis.context: Prevents confirmation bias and aimless 'browsing' across large data lakes.

elastic_common_schema.title: Elastic Common Schema (ECS)
elastic_common_schema.definition: An open-source specification that standardizes field names (such as destination.ip, source.bytes, event.dataset) across disparate log sources.
elastic_common_schema.context: Allows a single threat hunting query to search across Zeek, Suricata, Windows event logs, and firewall streams.

least_frequency_analysis.title: Least-Frequency Analysis (Long Tail)
least_frequency_analysis.definition: A threat hunting technique that aggregates events by cardinality and sorts by lowest occurrence to surface the rarest 0.01% of outbound connections.
least_frequency_analysis.context: Adversaries trying to avoid noise often blend into the long tail rather than high-volume aggregates.

terms_aggregation.title: Terms Aggregation
terms_aggregation.definition: An Elasticsearch multi-bucket query that groups documents by unique field values and calculates bucket metrics (e.g. unique host counts per IP).
terms_aggregation.context: Essential for stacking millions of connection records into inspectable frequency tables without pulling raw documents.
